chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Lester Young's brief stint in Fletcher's band
summary: Young joined Fletcher in Detroit playing high like an alto; some bandsmen didn't like him and gave him no room, which they later regretted.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: -- come out like this with the handkerchief and all -- "What do you say there, pops," you know? But Pres was playing -- he just lifted that band. And do you know he was with Fletcher's band, and he didn't sound like that. And I don't know if it was the style or whatnot, but he joined Fletcher's band in Detroit, Michigan.
He did? I didn't know that.

Yeah. And he was playing way up in the register then, and he sounded a lot like an alto, you know, maybe to some of the guys in the band, and funny thing about it, some of the guys in the band didn't dig him. That
was funny, you know, because I knew this guy, man, could play. And they regretted it many a day since then, including Fletcher, you know.

But they had some set guys in that band, you know, and they didn't give Pres a chance to stretch out. And, of course, certain tunes show off musicians, you know, better than others, you know, and I think this was actually one of the factors -- but he made up for it finally.
